gh pr create --base main --title "APRV-365: the app-server is this process's own child, and the claim says so" --body "**APRV-365** — custody of the socket, answered: there is no socket.

The bridge already starts the app-server as its own child over stdio pipes. Nothing binds a path and no other process holds a descriptor to speak on, so the replay of a pending request to whatever connects next cannot arise inside one run. Custody is the operating system's, which is the strongest kind available and the only kind this project would not have to attest. AC1 is satisfied by its first arm; what this PR adds is the statement of it and a claim scoped to what it makes true.

### What changed

- A custody section in the \`src/cli/codex-bridge.ts\` module header.
- Follow-up 5 in \`docs/codex-app-server-bridge.md\` marked landed, with the answer.
- A custody paragraph in the bridge section of \`docs/cli-reference.md\`.
- Three lines in the verb's help.
- **The claim moved everywhere it appears**: from \"this client decided every question it was asked\" to \"this client decided every question this app-server child asked in this session\". A Codex started outside this arrangement is a different process with a different connection, and nothing here observes it.

### Deliberately not built

A refusal of a server command that would attach to something already running, on the orchestrator's ruling. It needs a guess at another program's command line, which this repository has no record of, and a check written against a guessed shape finds nothing while reporting that it looked. The doc says the property is true and says where it stops holding.

### Schema change / protected path / conformance bump

None, none, none.
